title: Theo and the Contact
premise: Felix Dunmore, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Group—a diplomatic front that officially does not exist—receives calls on a burner phone from her mentor, Elias Voss, who died eighteen months ago. The voice warns of an attack at a Geneva summit engineered to look like an industrial accident, and reveals Felix was chosen for this case precisely because she is expendable. As she follows the phone's breadcrumbs, she uncovers that Meridian's director, Annelise Kade, sanctioned the attack to protect a blackmail network built on decades of 'attributed' operations—including one that killed Voss. In the end, Felix exposes Kade to the summit's security council, chooses love over the duty that made her invisible by going public with her testimony, and learns the caller was Voss's daughter, who inherited his files and his war.
about_author: M. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former policy analyst who spent six years inside international regulatory bodies before turning to fiction. Eriksen writes thrillers about the machinery behind official silence and lives between Oslo and Lisbon.

chapters.title: The Number That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She cleans up a diplomat's indiscretion in Vienna, erasing a woman and a memory card from existence, and returns to her anonymous flat feeling the weight of her own erasure. That night, a burner phone she never bought rings in her coat pocket. The emotional beat: professional detachment cracking into unease.

chapters.title: A Voice from the Cold
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The caller speaks in Elias Voss's cadence—her dead mentor—and names a date: the Geneva energy summit, eleven days out. She runs the number through every database; it has no origin. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into suspicion—someone is using her love for Voss as bait.

chapters.title: Meridian House Rules
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At Meridian's unmarked London office, Director Annelise Kade assigns her a routine protection detail for the summit, too neatly timed after the call. Felix notices Kade's aide flinch when Geneva is mentioned. Emotional beat: the first cold realization that her employer may be scripting her.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Answers
chapters.summary: Mira Voss's POV. Introduced in a Rotterdam safehouse, Mira maintains her father's encrypted archive and admits she has been calling Felix using voice synthesis trained on his recordings. She offers proof of the plot—but only face to face. Emotional beat: defiant inheritance; Mira refuses to let her father's death stay tidy.

chapters.title: Rotterdam, Off the Books
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She flies commercial under a false name and meets Mira, who shows her schematics of the summit's cooling plant and a maintenance contract signed by a shell company Felix recognizes—one she laundered for Meridian two years ago. Emotional beat: horror as her own past work surfaces in the enemy's blueprint.

chapters.title: What the Fixer Fixed
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with a flashback to the laundering job. She traces the shell company, Halcyon Utilities, and finds its beneficial owner is a trust controlled by Kade's family office. Doubt becomes evidence. Emotional beat: betrayal settling in like cold water—the institution she served built the bomb's cover.

chapters.title: Tail Lights on the Amstel
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Leaving Mira's safehouse, Felix spots a surveillance team and leads them on a chase through Amsterdam rather than lead them back. She loses them but realizes Meridian flagged her travel within hours. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve; invisibility is now a liability.

chapters.title: Kade's Quiet Offer
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Summoned to a private dinner, Kade offers Felix promotion, a named identity, a life above ground—if she delivers 'the Voss material' and stops asking about Geneva. Kade mentions Felix's estranged sister by name. Emotional beat: temptation and threat braided together; power showing its gentlest, most corrupting face.

chapters.title: Love Against the Ledger
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Mira and Felix grow close while decrypting Voss's archive in a canal house; Mira reveals her father discovered the plot and died for it, staged as a heart attack. Felix lets herself want something besides survival. Emotional beat: tenderness as risk—love becoming the reason to fight instead of flee.

chapters.title: The Archive Speaks
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The decrypted files reveal Operation LANTERN: a plan to trigger a coolant failure at the summit, killing delegates and blaming a contractor, thereby burying blackmail leverage over three governments. One file lists the fixer who enabled it: F. Dunmore. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into accountability.

chapters.title: Burn Notice, Unofficial
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Meridian freezes her accounts and revokes her covers; her sister receives an anonymous visit from 'welfare officers.' Felix understands Kade is tightening the noose. Emotional beat: isolation at full pressure—everything she built to disappear is being used to trap her.

chapters.title: Six Days in Geneva
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She and Mira reach Geneva and case the summit venue, mapping the cooling plant against LANTERN's schematics. They identify the insider: plant chief engineer Tomas Reiner, a blackmailed widower. Emotional beat: dread made concrete—the attack now has faces and a countdown.

chapters.title: Turning the Engineer
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix confronts Reiner privately, offering him exposure of his blackmailers and a path to immunity if he feeds false telemetry to the plotters. He breaks, agrees. Emotional beat: cautious hope—the first piece of the machine turned against itself.

chapters.title: The Leak Inside
chapters.summary: Reiner's POV. Reiner reports to his handler as instructed, but the handler's questions reveal Meridian knows about a leak—and suspects Felix. Reiner must choose which master to betray. Emotional beat: terror of a small man caught between giants, choosing conscience at cost.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Jet d'Eau
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A meet with a sympathetic summit security officer is a trap; Felix escapes wounded while Mira is taken. Kade calls: the archive for Mira, or both die as terrorists. Emotional beat: despair and fury—love against duty now means trading truth for a life.

chapters.title: The Trade That Isn't
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix prepares to surrender the archive but secretly seeds it with a dead-man switch routed to three journalists and the summit's independent oversight panel. She walks into the exchange knowing Kade will kill her anyway. Emotional beat: calm fatalism—duty redefined as making the truth unkillable.

chapters.title: Two Days to Zero
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Held in a Meridian black site outside Geneva, Mira stalls her interrogators and copies a drive left carelessly in the room. She learns the attack timeline moved up: tomorrow night. Emotional beat: resourceful defiance under fear; inheritance becomes action.

chapters.title: Night Shift at the Cooling Plant
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On attack night, Reiner feeds false readings while Felix infiltrates the plant to physically disable the fail-safe bypass. Kade's operational team arrives early. Emotional beat: breathless momentum—the accident begins assembling itself around them.

chapters.title: LANTERN, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Climax, Felix's POV. Felix triggers a controlled shutdown that makes the sabotage visible rather than catastrophic, forcing an evacuation that saves the delegates and exposes tampering. She confronts Kade in the control room; Kade offers everything one last time. Felix declines and records her refusal. Emotional beat: the moral climax—power offered and refused.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Rather than vanish, Felix gives sworn testimony to the oversight panel, naming Meridian, Kade, and her own role in building the cover network. The dead-man switch releases the archive worldwide. Emotional beat: costly redemption—visibility as penance and victory.

chapters.title: Aftermaths and Aliases
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Kade is detained pending trial; Meridian is formally dissolved; Reiner testifies under protection. Felix, officially a whistleblower and unofficially a target, plans disappearance on her own terms this time—with Mira. Emotional beat: bittersweet freedom; love chosen over the duty that consumed Voss.

chapters.title: The Phone Rings Once More
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Felix's POV. Months later in Lisbon, a new burner arrives in the mail. It rings once. On the line: not Voss's synthesized voice, but a stranger warning of another name, another city—implying LANTERN had siblings. Felix looks at Mira and answers. Emotional beat: open-ended vigilance; the fixer becomes the hunter.
